guide.title: Feature Guide
guide.ui_no_match: No topic has those words. Try a shorter word.
guide.ui_need_helper: No helper is here yet, so there is nobody to talk to.
guide.ui_help_hint: Every feature and how to use it, in plain words.
guide.what_1: Vanilla Agents shows your Claude Code sessions as heroes in a World of Warcraft inn. Every session is one helper, and its work shows up as quests.
guide.what_2: Nothing in the inn is pretend. A quest is a real piece of work, and it only counts as done after the checker has run your project's real tests.
guide.what_3: Everything runs on your own PC. The game art is baked from your own copy of WoW 1.12 and never leaves it.
guide.setup_1: Run setup.cmd once and drop your WoW 1.12 Data folder on it (the folder that holds patch.MPQ). It bakes the game art, connects Claude Code and puts a shortcut on your Desktop.
guide.setup_2: You need Python 3.10 or newer. If it is missing, setup.cmd opens the download page for you.
guide.setup_3: Tip: the first bake takes a few minutes. You only do it once per PC.
guide.launch_1: Double-click vanilla-agents.cmd or the Desktop shortcut. A window with the inn opens. Close the window to quit.
guide.launch_2: Just want to look around? Run demo.cmd. Six pretend helpers work through a few quests, and nothing real is changed.
guide.launch_3: Each time it starts, the launcher quietly checks that Claude still points at this folder, so moving the folder is safe.
guide.first_1: Start any Claude Code session. A hero walks into the inn and sits down at a laptop.
guide.first_2: When its work becomes a quest, the Quest Log shows it. Approve it if you agree, or ask for a change.
guide.first_3: Click the hero to talk to it. Esc opens the Game Menu and F1 opens Help. This guide can be opened from both.
guide.project_1: A project is a folder with your code (a git repository). The window shows one project at a time.
guide.project_2: Press Esc, then Log Out, to choose a project. Pick one from the list, or type a folder and press Open.
guide.project_3: A folder you have never used? Type it and press Add project. Vanilla Agents works out what kind of project it is and sets up its checks.
guide.project_4: Tip: the Flight Master (F) switches between projects you already added.
guide.help_window_1: F1 opens Help: every key, how to move, how to get started, the version and the licences.
guide.help_window_2: The big Feature guide button at the top of Help opens this guide.
guide.help_window_3: Save diagnostics writes a plain text file you can share when you ask someone for help.
guide.move_1: W and S walk forward and back, A and D turn, Q and E step sideways, and Space jumps.
guide.move_2: Hold Shift to walk slowly. Num Lock keeps you running until you press W or S.
guide.move_3: Hold the right mouse button and drag to turn. Hold the left button and drag to look around. The mouse wheel zooms in and out.
guide.move_4: Tip: movement keys do nothing while you type in a box, so chatting is safe.
guide.emotes_1: Press X to sit on the floor, and X again to stand up.
guide.emotes_2: Type an emote in the chat line, like /dance, /wave, /cheer, /bow, /sleep, /kneel or /sit, and your character plays it.
guide.emotes_4: To choose who you play as, open Esc > Options > Vanilla Agents > Choose Character.
guide.select_1: Click a hero to select it. The camera turns to it, it waves, and its talk window opens.
guide.select_2: If the hero sits at a laptop, the camera looks over its shoulder so you can read its screen.
guide.select_3: Press Esc to let go of the selected hero.
guide.laptops_1: Working helpers sit at the inn's tables with a laptop. The lid opens when they sit down and shuts when they get up.
guide.laptops_2: The laptop screen fills with what the helper is doing right now, line by line, with a blinking cursor.
guide.laptops_3: When every table seat is taken, helpers use the desks along the walls.
guide.errands: What helpers do in the inn
guide.errands_1: While they work, helpers run errands: reading at a bookshelf when they look things up, and sitting by the fire to think when it goes quiet.
guide.errands_2: When a helper runs tests or a build, it hammers at the anvil or forge while more tests follow (no anvil in this inn: it stands by its laptop and works). When it commits, pushes, publishes or zips its work, it carries a sack to the crates.
guide.errands_3: A helper that waits for your answer, or whose quest is handed in, waits at the quest board and asks now and then until you decide. Click the board to open the Quest Log. While the checker tests its quest, it hammers at the anvil.
guide.errands_4: They cheer once when a check of their quest passes, shake their head when a step fails and go down on one knee when a check fails. When the jukebox plays, they dance. Reduce motion stops the errands and emotes.
guide.errands_5: Candles, lanterns and chandeliers glow and flicker softly, brightest at night. How many glow depends on Render quality; when the inn runs slowly they are switched off first.
guide.ghosts: Ghosts, going home and stunned helpers
guide.ghosts_1: A helper that has been quiet for 15 minutes turns into a ghost. It comes back to life as soon as it works again.
guide.ghosts_2: When a Claude session ends, its helper walks home and leaves the inn.
guide.ghosts_3: A grey dots sign over a head means Claude's service stopped that session, for example at a usage limit or after an error. The helper looks dazed until it acts again.
guide.minimap_1: The round map at the top right shows this floor from above. You are the arrow.
guide.minimap_2: Gold dots are working helpers, grey dots are waiting ones and blue dots are ghosts.
guide.minimap_3: The map turns with your camera, like in the game.
guide.jukebox_1: J plays or pauses the jukebox, and K skips to the next song.
guide.jukebox_2: The music fits the building you picked. Turn off Building music in the options to hear every song you baked.
guide.views: Inn, drawn workshop and photo mode
guide.views_1: The 3D inn is the main view. On a PC that cannot show 3D, a simple drawn workshop appears instead, with all the same windows.
guide.views_2: If the inn runs slowly for a while, render quality goes down by itself and Help tells you. You can set it back in the options.
guide.views_3: There is also a photo mode for showcase pictures. It is a tool for developers and has no button.
guide.who_1: Every Claude Code session is one helper. It gets a name, a race and a look that stay the same.
guide.who_2: Sessions with the hooks show up right away. Without hooks, Vanilla Agents still finds sessions by reading Claude's own session files, with less detail.
guide.who_3: Background sessions that Claude runs on its own also appear, marked as background.
guide.raid_1: The raid frames list every helper: portrait, name, small icons, a green bar for quests passed and a blue bar for the memory (mana) it has left.
guide.raid_2: Click a frame to select that helper. Double-click it to open its talk window.
guide.raid_3: Helpers working on the same quest sit together under a small gold header with the quest's name.
guide.needs_1: When Claude asks for permission or has a question, its helper shows a gold ! over its head and its raid frame pulses.
guide.needs_2: You also hear a sound, the window title shows a count in the taskbar, and when the window is in the background you get a desktop notification.
guide.needs_3: Go to that Claude Code session and answer it. The ! goes away when the helper acts again.
guide.needs_4: Tip: your first click in the window asks once whether notifications are allowed.
guide.auras_1: Small icons on the raid frames and the player frame show what is going on: checks running, paused, failed, blocked or verified, and quests approved or auto-approved.
guide.auras_2: Icons with a green edge are good news (buffs). Icons with a red edge are problems (debuffs). Hover an icon to read what it means.
guide.clash_1: All helpers share one copy of your project. When two of them change the same file within 15 minutes, both raid frames show a warning sign.
guide.clash_2: The talk window shows a red line with the file and the other helper's name.
guide.clash_3: Tip: ask one of them to wait, or give them different parts of the work.
guide.mana_1: A helper's blue bar is its mana: how much room is left in its conversation memory. Full means fresh.
guide.mana_2: With the status line bridge on, the bar uses Claude's real numbers, and the player frame's blue bar shows your 5-hour plan limit and when it resets.
guide.mana_3: When a helper tidies up its memory, its mana fills up again and it has a drink.
guide.charsheet_1: C opens the selected helper's character sheet: its face, level, experience, pass rate and the tools it used.
guide.charsheet_2: Level and experience come from work done. Every ten actions make a level.
guide.charsheet_3: The task timeline shows what it did, what it is doing and what comes next. Force Play runs the checks now, and the arrows switch to the helper of another step.
guide.talents_1: T opens a talent tree for the selected helper. It only shows things; you cannot spend points.
guide.talents_2: Tools has one talent per tool it used. Trust shows how its quests were approved. Results shows quests and checks passed or failed, and quests waiting for you.
guide.talents_3: What a helper may do is set in Claude's own permissions, not here.
guide.inspect_1: N opens Inspect: the project's changed files, worn as gear. The colour shows how big a change is, and the letter what kind it is.
guide.inspect_2: Click a file to read what changed, line by line.
guide.inspect_3: In a talk window, Show me your changes opens Inspect with only that helper's files. Show all brings back everything.
guide.quest_1: A quest is one piece of work, with a plain title and a reason. Helpers add quests themselves, and you can post your own.
guide.quest_2: A gold ! is new, a grey ? is in progress and a gold ? is ready to hand in. After the checks it is complete, failed, or out of range when it got stuck.
guide.questlog_1: L opens the Quest Log. Click a quest to see its objectives, why it matters, how big and how risky it is, and which check route it takes.
guide.questlog_2: The buttons under a quest are your decision: Approve, Change or Investigate.
guide.questlog_3: Tip: a quest that got finished in another way is marked as done elsewhere.
guide.approve_1: Approve says yes: the helper may go ahead with this work.
guide.approve_2: Change sends a short note about what should be different. Investigate asks the helper to explain the quest in plain words; the answer appears under the quest.
guide.approve_3: Only you can approve. A helper can never approve its own work.
guide.tiers_1: Small, low-risk quests may start by themselves. They say Auto-approved and why. Press Undo the yes if you do not agree.
guide.tiers_2: Some quests never start by themselves, like publishing, spending real money or deleting things. They always wait for you.
guide.tiers_3: Big or risky quests always ask you first.
guide.loot: Loot rolls: Need, Greed and Pass
guide.loot_1: When a quest is ready and you have not approved it yet, a loot roll pops up above the action bar.
guide.loot_2: Need means Approve. Greed means ask for a change (type a few words). Pass hides the roll for now.
guide.loot_3: The timer only hides the roll. It never decides anything for you.
guide.bounty: Bounty Board: post your own quest
guide.bounty_1: H opens the Bounty Board. Bounties are quests no helper has taken yet. Taken shows who is working on what.
guide.bounty_2: Use Post a bounty to add your own quest: a short title and why it matters. A helper can pick it up.
guide.idea_1: I opens the Idea: what the project is for, what it must not become, what done means, and places that are hands off.
guide.idea_2: It is drafted once when you add a project. Read it and press Approve. Change it whenever your goals change.
guide.idea_3: If a helper changes a file in a hands-off place, the chat and the Quest Log show an Intent check line.
guide.dailies_1: Daily quests are quests the window posts by itself once a day, for example a weekly tidy-up or a check of the backups.
guide.dailies_2: They are off until you turn them on. Ask a helper to set them up in app.json under daily: a title, a reason, a time and the days.
guide.away_1: The window only listens to this PC. Away from it, you can talk to a Claude session that runs on this PC, for example from your phone.
guide.away_2: That session can approve or pause a quest for you with scripts/decide.py. It is recorded as you, via a phone session.
guide.away_3: There is also a small read-only page, phone.html, at the window's address. It shows helpers and quests in a narrow layout.
guide.checker_1: The checker runs your project's real tests after a quest is handed in. Only when they pass is the quest complete.
guide.checker_2: Some checks are hidden from the helpers, so nobody can write work that only fools the tests.
guide.checker_3: When a check fails, the quest is sent back with the evidence, so the helper knows what to fix.
guide.verify_1: V, or Verify now on the action bar, runs the checks right away. The cast bar fills while a check runs.
guide.verify_2: Tip: the Spellbook, Force Play on the character sheet and Run the checks in a talk window do the same thing.
guide.pause_1: Z, or Pause on the action bar, puts the checker on hold. The player frame shows PAUSED in red and gold.
guide.pause_2: Press it again (Resume) to carry on. Pausing also stops a check that is running.
guide.hearth_1: Hearth on the action bar is the emergency stop. It pauses the checker and whispers every helper to stop and wait.
guide.hearth_2: Click it twice to be sure. Each helper sees the whisper at its next step.
guide.route_1: A small change takes the fast route: only the quick checks. Big changes, build files and the checker's own files take the full route, hidden checks included.
guide.route_2: The Quest Log says which route a quest takes, and why.
guide.castbar_1: While a check runs, a bar in the middle of the screen fills up with the check's name. It opens by itself.
guide.castbar_2: The bar is a guess from how long the check usually takes. It never fills up before the check has really finished.
guide.spellbook_1: P opens the Spellbook. Each check of your project is a spell, and its mark shows the last result.
guide.spellbook_2: Click a spell to run the checks now. A dark clock sweeps over it while it runs.
guide.backpack_1: B opens the backpack: checker reports and the files your helpers changed, shown as items.
guide.backpack_2: The border colour is the result: green passed, red text failed, grey got stuck, white is still running or is a file.
guide.worldmap_1: M opens the World Map: your project's folders drawn as zones on parchment.
guide.worldmap_2: Fog means nobody has touched it yet. Explored means a helper worked there. Cleared means the whole project passed its checks after the last change there.
guide.worldmap_3: Hover a zone to see its files and who was there.
guide.gossip_1: Click a hero, or double-click its raid frame, to open its talk window. It tells you in its own voice what it is doing.
guide.gossip_2: Pick what to ask: what it is working on, show me your changes, explain this quest, I want something changed, run the checks, or whisper.
guide.gossip_3: Claude's own to-do list for that session is shown here too.
guide.follow: Follow me, Take a break, Are you still there?
guide.follow_1: Follow me makes a helper walk after you around the inn. Stop following me ends it.
guide.follow_2: Take a break sends a helper that is not working to a seat or to the fire.
guide.follow_3: Are you still there? whispers a quiet, waiting or stunned helper to check on it.
guide.whispers_1: A whisper is a short message to one helper. It reads it at its next step and answers in pink, in the chat and in the talk window.
guide.whispers_2: Whisper from the talk window, or type /w and the helper's name and your message in the chat line.
guide.whispers_3: Type /p and a message (or /party) to whisper every helper at once.
guide.chatline: The chat line and its commands
guide.chatline_1: Press Enter to start typing in the chat line. Enter sends, Esc stops typing.
guide.chatline_2: /w name message whispers one helper. /p message talks to all your helpers. /c message talks to the people in your party (Community chat).
guide.chatline_3: Emotes such as /dance, /wave, /cheer, /sit, /sleep and /kneel play on your own character.
guide.chat_1: The chat tells you everything that happens, in plain words. Each colour is a speaker: the system, helpers, the checker, and pink whispers.
guide.chat_2: The filter list shows all lines, only helpers, only system lines, only the checker, or only one helper.
guide.chat_3: Type in the Search box to keep only lines with those words. Matches are marked, and Esc clears the search.
guide.mailbox_1: O opens the Mailbox. A letter arrives for each finished check, each quest that passes or fails, each whisper answer, and a summary once a day.
guide.mailbox_2: Letters stay after their chat line has scrolled away. Delete the ones you have read.
guide.mailbox_3: The small mail button under the player frame tells you when new mail has arrived.
guide.win_basics_1: Each window has a key (see the Keyboard reference). Press it again, or click the red x, to close the window.
guide.win_basics_2: Esc closes the window you opened last. With nothing open, Esc opens the Game Menu.
guide.win_basics_3: The window you clicked last comes to the front.
guide.unitframes_1: Top left is you, the Controller. The gold bar counts quests done. The blue bar shows usage, or your plan limit when the status line bridge is on.
guide.unitframes_2: Next to it, the target frame shows the selected helper. An achievement title you earned shows under your name.
guide.monitor_1: It shows how many helpers are working, whether the window still hears new events (LIVE or OFFLINE), and what the checker is doing.
guide.monitor_2: Tip: OFFLINE for a long time usually means the program was closed. See Troubleshooting.
guide.actionbar_1: The bar at the bottom has six buttons, on the keys 1 to 6 like the game's action bar: Verify now, Pause (Resume while paused), Needs you, Quest log, Changes and Hearth.
guide.actionbar_2: Needs you goes to the next helper with a gold "!" (press it again for the one after) and shows how many are waiting. Hover a button to see what it does. Hearth needs two presses. V, Z, L and N still work too.
guide.meters_1: U opens the damage meter: one bar per helper, in its class colour.
guide.meters_2: The tabs show actions per minute, total actions, quests passed, the combat log of tool and checker lines, and Cost.
guide.meters_3: Cost is each session's cost as Claude Code estimates it, also per minute. It needs the status line bridge.
guide.achievements_1: Y opens Achievements: small goals such as a streak of passed quests, five helpers at once or a flawless run.
guide.achievements_2: A new one shows a gold banner, and its title appears under your name.
guide.replay_1: R opens Replay, a time machine above the action bar. Drag the slider to see the whole window as it was at that moment.
guide.replay_2: Play runs time forward and the speed button makes it faster. Live brings you back to now.
guide.replay_3: While you look at the past, new events wait for you and appear when you press Live.
guide.flight_1: F opens the Flight Master. Every project you added is a flight point, and You are here marks the open one.
guide.flight_2: Click a point and press Fly to switch to that project.
guide.escmenu_1: Esc opens the Game Menu: Options, Guide, Log Out (choose or add a project), Exit Game and Return to Game.
guide.escmenu_2: Support and Macros are greyed out because they are not part of Vanilla Agents.
guide.guide_window_1: Open the guide from Help (F1), from the Game Menu (Guide) or with the ? button in the Options window.
guide.guide_window_2: Type in the search box to find a topic. An Open it button opens the window the topic is about, and Show in Options jumps to the setting.
guide.party_1: G opens the Party window, where you play together with other people and their Claude helpers. Everyone's helpers walk around in your inn.
guide.party_2: One person hosts and sends the invite link. The others paste it and press Join.
guide.hosting_1: Choose who can join: Only this PC (to try it out) or My network (friends on your Wi-Fi or VPN).
guide.hosting_2: Invite links run out after 1 hour to 3 days (24 hours unless you change it). New link makes a fresh one and stops the old one.
guide.hosting_3: Only the host can make a new link or remove someone (press Remove twice). Share links only with friends.
guide.plan_1: Anyone can propose items: what, why and how big. Your Claude can suggest items too.
guide.plan_2: When everyone who is active presses I agree on the same version, the plan locks and is shared out fairly by size.
guide.plan_3: Your items become quests in your own Quest Log, and you still approve them yourself. Before work starts, you can Take an item from someone.
guide.community_1: The Chat window has two tabs. General is the usual log; Community is a chat with the people in your party only, like a guild chat.
guide.community_2: Click the Community tab and type, or type /c and your message from any tab. Your own name is highlighted, and a red number on the tab counts lines you have not read.
guide.community_3: Community lines are never sent to Claude: they are not in the event feed, the tools or the helpers' messages. The host keeps the last 300 lines and can delete a line (the small x on hover).
guide.party_shares_1: Names, helper names and roles, working or idle, a one-line activity, the plan and its statuses.
guide.party_shares_2: Never your code, files, window key or approvals. Leaving the party stops all of it.
guide.zones_1: Press F3 (or Esc > Zones & Inns, or the button under the Flight Master map) to see every inn you can work in, by zone: 17 zones of Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire to the Gadgetzan Inn.
guide.zones_2: Pick a zone on the left to see its map with every area explored. Its inns show as cards with a picture of the inside, taken the first time you visit. Travel here moves your inn there.
guide.zones_3: Each zone has the game's own light outside the windows, from its lighting tables at the inn's town (cold in Dun Morogh, blue gloom in Duskwood, warm haze in Tanaris), plus its own music and loading screen. Time of day Auto follows your clock smoothly.
guide.buildings_1: Thirteen buildings from the game: the Goldshire Inn with three furniture sets, Darkshire, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, Moonbrook, a town hall, a guild house, a mage tower, an orc inn, a night elf inn and Ratchet.
guide.buildings_2: In each building, helpers find their own desks and seats.
guide.own_building_1: Put a .glb model file in the office folder inside your assets folder. It appears in the building picker as yours.
guide.own_building_2: Mark desks, seats, the fire and the quest board with empties called desk_1, seat_1, fire and board. docs/OFFICE.md has the details.
guide.own_building_3: Give the screen of each PC in your model its own material called Screen: it shows, live, the page of the helper at the nearest desk, and a dim screensaver while that desk is free.
guide.timeofday_1: The light follows your clock unless you choose otherwise. Pick day, dusk or night to keep it fixed.
guide.hooks_1: Hooks are short notes Claude Code sends at every step. Setup installs them, and they never slow down or block a session.
guide.hooks_2: To check that it works, start a Claude Code session and watch a new hero walk in.
guide.hooks_3: uninstall.cmd removes them again. Your Claude settings are backed up first.
guide.tools_1: Claude also gets tools: see the quests, start a quest, report progress, hand a quest in, read and answer your requests, reply to whispers, take a quest, and see or suggest party plan items.
guide.tools_2: Approving, checking, pausing and marking work done are not tools. They stay yours.
guide.tools_3: Setup installs the tools for Claude Code and for the Claude desktop app. Restart the desktop app afterwards.
guide.plugin_1: The plugin folder packs the hooks and the tools as one Claude Code plugin. Use the plugin or the installers, not both.
guide.plugin_2: docs/PLUGIN.md has the two commands that install it.
guide.statusline_1: This is optional. It sends Claude's real numbers to the window: memory used, session cost, lines changed and your plan limits.
guide.statusline_2: Turn it on with python scripts/install_statusline.py (or run setup with --statusline). Your old status line keeps showing.
guide.statusline_3: It powers the real mana bars, the plan limit on the player frame and the Cost tab of the damage meter.
guide.background_1: If the claude command is installed, the window asks it every 15 seconds which sessions are running, and shows the ones the hooks have not reported yet.
guide.background_2: They are marked as background, and they still show when they wait for you or fail.
guide.answers_1: Helpers see your whispers and your Change and Investigate requests at their next step, together with the exact way to answer.
guide.answers_2: Their answers show under the quest, in the chat and in the talk window.
guide.reconnect_1: Claude remembers where the hooks and tools live. vanilla-agents.cmd fixes that by itself every time it starts.
guide.reconnect_2: It only changes entries you installed before, and it keeps a backup.
guide.options_1: Esc > Options opens the Options window. Categories are on the left and choices on the right. Hover any choice to see what it does.
guide.options_2: Vanilla Agents' own choices are under Vanilla Agents. Each one has a short line that says what it does and when to change it.
guide.options_3: The search box finds a choice by name. Defaults puts the page back to its first values. Every change is saved in this browser at once.
guide.game_options_1: Interface, Video and Sound Options come from the game itself, so the window feels like WoW. They are saved, but most of them do not change Vanilla Agents.
guide.game_options_2: Master volume and the sound on or off switch do change the window's sounds.
guide.set_building_1: Where your helpers work. Changing it reloads the page into the new building.
guide.set_building_2: Change it when you want a different look or music.
guide.set_time_1: The light in the building. Auto follows your clock.
guide.set_time_2: Pick a fixed time if you like one look best.
guide.set_music_1: On: the jukebox plays music that fits the building. Off: it plays every song you baked.
guide.set_quality_1: How sharp the inn is drawn, from Low to High.
guide.set_quality_2: Go lower if the inn feels slow or jerky. Go higher on a strong PC for smoother edges.
guide.set_fps_1: The most pictures per second the inn draws: 30, 60 or no cap.
guide.set_fps_2: Pick 30 on a laptop to save battery and keep the fans quiet.
guide.set_helpers_1: How many helpers walk around in the inn, from 1 to 15. Everyone still shows in the raid frames.
guide.set_helpers_2: Lower it when the inn gets crowded or slow.
guide.set_motion_1: Stops emotes, sparks, camera sway, errands and the pulsing raid frame. It starts out the same as your system's reduce motion setting.
guide.set_motion_2: Turn it on if movement on screen bothers you.
guide.set_character_1: Pick the hero you walk around as in the inn. The list is grouped by race.
guide.sound_1: Esc > Options > Vanilla Agents > Sound: master volume, mute, and one sound for each event, such as a helper finishing, a quest passing or failing, a helper needing you or mana running low.
guide.sound_2: For each event, pick a sound, set its volume, switch it on or off and press Test to hear it. Changes are saved at once.
guide.sound_3: The Helpers switch is kept for starting extra Claude workers from the window. This version does not start any, so it changes nothing yet.
guide.files_1: A few settings live in files instead of the window: daily quests, background sessions, the port and the folders searched for projects.
guide.files_2: docs/CHANGE-GUIDE.md lists every one of them. Ask a helper to change one, then restart the window.
guide.local_1: The window answers only this PC. No accounts, no tracking and no update checks.
guide.local_2: Claude's events go to a file in the .vanilla-agents folder in your user folder, and only this program reads it.
guide.windowkey_1: The window's address carries a secret key. Every change, like approving, needs it.
guide.windowkey_2: Whoever has that link can approve things, so never share it.
guide.owner_1: Helpers can start quests, report progress and hand in work. They can never approve, run or pause the checks, or mark work as done.
guide.owner_2: In a party too, nobody can approve your quests for you.
guide.addons_1: Addons are small scripts that run inside the window, like WoW addons: a sign, a counter, a new little window. Open them from Game Menu > AddOns or Options > Vanilla Agents.
guide.addons_2: An addon can press any button you can, whatever it says it does, so only enable addons you wrote or trust. New ones start switched off. docs/ADDONS.md shows how to write one.
guide.backups_1: Once a day, the open project's quest history is copied into its state/backups folder. The last seven copies are kept.
guide.a11y_1: Tab moves between buttons and boxes, and a gold ring shows where you are. Keys never fire while a button has keyboard focus.
guide.a11y_2: Screen readers hear new chat lines and banners, and every window has a name.
guide.a11y_3: Reduce motion stops emotes, sparks, camera sway and the pulsing raid frame.
guide.rebake: Some game art is out of date
guide.rebake_1: A red banner says some art is out of date. Press F1: the top of Help shows the exact command.
guide.rebake_2: Close the window, run that command in the data folder, then start Vanilla Agents again.
guide.no_helpers_1: Start a new Claude Code session after setup. Sessions that were already running do not pick up the hooks.
guide.no_helpers_2: Moved the folder? Start with vanilla-agents.cmd so it reconnects Claude.
guide.no_helpers_3: Still missing? Check Helpers in the building in the options. Everyone always shows in the raid frames.
guide.empty_inn_1: No helpers means no Claude Code session has started yet. Just looking? Run demo.cmd.
guide.offline_1: The chat says it lost the connection and keeps trying again. Usually the program was closed. Start it again and the window catches up.
guide.slow_1: Lower Render quality, set the frame rate cap to 30, show fewer helpers and turn on Reduce motion.
guide.slow_2: Tip: the window already lowers quality by itself when it stays slow for a while.
guide.no3d_1: If your PC cannot show 3D, the drawn workshop appears instead. Updating your graphics driver usually brings the inn back.
guide.no3d_2: If the graphics driver resets, the window reloads by itself after a moment.
guide.diagnostics_1: Help (F1) > Save diagnostics writes a text file to your Desktop: versions, settings problems, what is baked and recent window errors.
guide.diagnostics_2: It contains no keys, code or quest text. Read it before you share it.
guide.uninstall_1: Run uninstall.cmd. It takes Vanilla Agents out of Claude Code and the Claude desktop app and removes the Desktop shortcut.
guide.uninstall_2: Then delete the .vanilla-agents folder in your user folder (game art, settings and history) and the Vanilla Agents folder itself.
guide.keys_windows_1: Press a key to open its window, and press it again to close it.
guide.keys_actions_1: These keys act right away or open the menus. The action bar answers to 1 to 6 as well.
guide.keys_moving_1: W A S D move and turn, Q and E step sideways, Space jumps, Shift walks, Num Lock keeps running and X sits.
guide.keys_moving_2: Mouse: right-drag turns, left-drag looks around, the wheel zooms and a click on a hero talks to it.
guide.keys_moving_3: There is no key for this guide, because every free letter is used for walking. Open it from Help (F1) or the Game Menu.
ws.game_note: These options come from World of Warcraft itself and are kept for the look. They are saved, but only the sound ones change Vanilla Agents. Your own settings are under Vanilla Agents.
guide.community_4: Outside a party the tab tells you how to join one (G). The search box above the chat searches the tab you are on.
guide.zones_4: Tick Always use this inn for the project to give a project its own zone: opening that project later takes you straight there, so every project is its own themed room.
guide.zones_5: No pictures yet? Take pictures of the inns without one visits each inn once and brings you back. Zone maps missing? In the data folder run: python -m vanilla_agents.assets bake places buildings
gossip.resurrect_ok: A new terminal is opening with {name}'s Claude session. When it says something, {name} is back.
gossip.resurrect_fail: Could not open it: {error} Type this in a terminal instead:
gossip.greet_left: I went home (my Claude session ended). Resurrect opens it again where I left off.
inspect.other_checkout: (another checkout: its changes are not in this list)
meter.tokens_empty: No token counts yet. They come from Claude's own session files once a helper writes something.
meter.tokens_body:
Tokens written per minute lately: {n}
Written so far (that Vanilla Agents has seen): {count}
help.phone_text: Approve, pause and check from your own phone on your home network, or get a message on Discord, Slack or ntfy when a helper needs you.
phone.unreachable: Not reachable ({error}). Is Vanilla Agents running, and Phone access on?
phone.need_key: Open the link from Options > Phone on your PC (scan its QR code). It carries the key.
phone.remote_pair_head: Pair this browser with your PC
phone.remote_pair_text: This link came from Options > Browser access on your PC. Give this browser a name you will recognise in the list there, then press Pair.
phone.remote_refused: That pairing link has expired or was already used. Make a new one on your PC (Options > Browser access).
phone.remote_no_link: Not paired yet. On your PC open Vanilla Agents, Options > Browser access, and scan or open the pairing link there.
phone.remote_old_browser: This browser cannot do the sealing Vanilla Agents needs (X25519). Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
phone.remote_pc_offline: Your PC is offline: Vanilla Agents is closed or Browser access is off.
phone.remote_respond: Watching, and you can approve, pause and verify
phone.remote_forget_ask: Forget this PC in this browser? You will need a new pairing link to come back.
phone.remote_sealed: End-to-end sealed: the relay passes messages on but cannot read them.
phonelink.title: Phone
phonelink.desc: See the inn on your phone and press Approve, Pause and Verify there. Your phone must be on the same home network (Wi-Fi) as this PC.
phonelink.toggle: Phone access (let my phone reach this window over my home network)
phonelink.warning: Anyone who has this link can approve quests, pause and run checks. Scan it only with your own phone, and switch Phone access off when you do not need it.
phonelink.off: Phone access is off: only this PC can open the window.
phonelink.scan: Scan with your phone's camera, or copy the link:
phonelink.fresh: The link changes every time Vanilla Agents starts.
phonelink.no_key: This window was opened without its key, so it cannot make the phone link. Open Vanilla Agents from its icon.
phonelink.qr_label: QR code of the phone link
browserlink.title: Browser access
browserlink.desc: See the inn from any browser, anywhere: a laptop at work, or your phone on mobile data. This PC connects out to the Open Vanilla relay; everything between this PC and your browsers is sealed, so the relay passes it on but cannot read it.
browserlink.toggle: Browser access (connect this PC to the relay)
browserlink.off: Browser access is off: no browser outside this PC can see the inn.
browserlink.respond_warning: A browser paired with Watch and approve can approve quests, pause and run checks. Pair only your own devices.
browserlink.scan: Open this link in the browser you want to pair (scan it with a phone's camera, or copy it):
browserlink.once: Works once, for {n} minutes. Then make a new one.
browserlink.qr_label: QR code of the pairing link
browserlink.claude_text: Bring a Claude that runs on the web (claude.ai, or Claude Code on the web) into your inn: make an address here, then in Claude add it as a custom connector (Settings > Connectors). That Claude shows up as a helper. It can start quests, report and ask, never approve.
browserlink.claude_note: Shown only now. Anyone with this address can post quests and progress to your inn; remove it below if it leaks.
browserlink.claude_none: No Claude connected this way yet.
notifyhub.title: Notifications
notifyhub.desc: Get a short message on your phone or chat when something needs you. Switch on the ones you use, choose what they tell you, then Save.
notifyhub.privacy: Only short plain sentences are sent, like "Varn needs you: permission for Bash" or "Quest done: Fix the login". Never code, files or commands. The links are kept in your own settings file on this PC.
notifyhub.discord_desc: A channel's webhook: Server settings > Integrations > Webhooks > New webhook > Copy webhook URL.
notifyhub.slack_desc: An incoming webhook from a Slack app (api.slack.com/apps > Incoming Webhooks).
notifyhub.ntfy_desc: Free push messages with the ntfy app (ntfy.sh). Pick a hard-to-guess topic name and subscribe to it in the app.
notifyhub.webhook_desc: Any address that takes a JSON POST with source, event, text and ts. For Home Assistant, IFTTT or your own scripts.
notifyhub.test_ok: Sent. Look for it on your phone.
chatreply.title: Chat replies
chatreply.desc: Answer from Discord, Slack or ntfy when you are away: whisper a helper, ask for the status, or pause. Vanilla Agents reads the channel every few seconds; no server on the internet is needed.
chatreply.privacy: Only people on your allow list are obeyed (ntfy: messages that start with your passphrase). Approvals, Verify, picking winners and settings stay in the window. Replies are short sentences, never code, files or paths. Tokens stay in your own settings file on this PC.
chatreply.demo: Developer demo: chat replies talk to a local fake server (VANILLA_CHAT_FAKE), not the real Discord, Slack or ntfy.
chatreply.discord_desc: A Discord bot you made (discord.com/developers: New Application > Bot > Reset Token, switch on Message Content Intent) and invited to your server with View Channel, Read Message History and Send Messages.
chatreply.slack_desc: A Slack app (api.slack.com/apps) with the bot scopes channels:history and chat:write, installed to your workspace and invited to the channel (/invite @your-app).
chatreply.ntfy_desc: Send a message to a reply topic in the ntfy app. ntfy does not know who you are, so every command starts with your passphrase, like pw123: status.
chatreply.slack_token_hint: xoxb-... (OAuth & Permissions > Bot User OAuth Token)
chatreply.secret_saved: Saved (ends in {word}). Leave empty to keep it.
chatreply.secret_saved_short: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
chatreply.discord_channel_hint: a long number: Developer Mode on, right-click the channel, Copy Channel ID
chatreply.discord_allow_hint: user ids, separated by commas (right-click yourself, Copy User ID)
chatreply.slack_allow_hint: member ids like U0123ABCD (profile > More > Copy member ID)
chatreply.passphrase_hint: a word only you know, no spaces or colon
chatreply.testing: Reading the channel and saying hello...
chatreply.test_ok: It works: read {name} and said hello there.
chatreply.ignored: Ignored {count} from people not on your list.
chatreply.commands: Commands: status · @Name message (or /w Name message) · /p message (or @everyone message) · pause / resume (when allowed) · help
guide.resurrect_1: A helper whose Claude session went quiet becomes a ghost; one whose session ended goes home and shows as a grey frame for two hours.
guide.resurrect_2: Talk to it and pick Resurrect, or right-click its raid frame. A new terminal opens with claude --resume in the helper's folder, and the helper rises in a golden light when it comes back.
guide.resurrect_3: No terminal or no claude command on this PC? The talk window shows the exact command to copy into one yourself.
guide.worktrees_1: Each helper's branch (and its git worktree, if it works in one) shows when you hover its raid frame, in the talk window's work view and in Inspect.
guide.worktrees_2: The same-file warning only appears for helpers in the same checkout: two helpers in different worktrees can change the same file safely.
guide.tokens_1: The damage meter (U) has a Tokens tab: how many words (tokens) each helper's Claude writes per minute, read from its own conversation file.
guide.tokens_2: It counts Claude's answers only, not what you send it. The Cost tab next to it needs the status line bridge.
guide.phone_1: Options > Phone (or Help > Phone link) switches on phone access. It is off until you turn it on.
guide.phone_2: When it is on, scan the QR code with your phone on the same home network. The phone page shows your helpers and quests, and lets you approve quests, pause and run the checks.
guide.phone_3: Anyone who has that link can approve work, so only open it on your own phone. Switch it off again with the same switch.
guide.phone_4: The phone link only works inside your home network, never from the internet.
guide.browser_1: Options > Browser access lets you see the inn from any browser, anywhere, not only at home. It is off until you switch it on.
guide.browser_2: Make a pairing link (Watch only, or Watch and approve) and open it in the browser you want to use. It works once.
guide.browser_3: Connect a Claude makes an address you paste into Claude as a connector, so a Claude on the web joins your inn as a helper.
guide.notifications_1: Options > Notifications sends short messages to Discord, Slack, ntfy or your own webhook when a helper needs you, a quest is ready or done, a check fails, a helper is stunned or the party agrees a plan.
guide.notifications_2: Paste the webhook link (or the ntfy topic), tick the events you want, press Send test, then Save.
guide.notifications_3: Only short sentences go out, like "Varn needs you: permission for Bash". Never code, file contents, paths or commands.
guide.notifications_4: The same message goes out at most once a minute, so a busy afternoon does not flood your phone.
guide.chatreplies: Answer from Discord, Slack or ntfy
guide.chatreplies_1: Options > Chat replies lets you talk back from your phone: in your own Discord or Slack channel (or an ntfy topic) type @Varn please add a test, /p stop and save, or status.
guide.chatreplies_2: Only the people on your allow list are obeyed; for ntfy every message starts with your passphrase, like pw123: status. Everyone else is ignored and counted in the status line.
guide.chatreplies_3: Chat can whisper, ask for the status and, if you tick it, pause or resume. It can never approve, verify, mark a quest done or change settings: those stay in the window and on the phone link.
guide.chatreplies_4: When a helper answers a whisper that came from chat, its answer goes back to that channel with its name, as short sentences without code or file names.
contest.title: Need or Greed
contest.head: {count} of {total} fixes in · the winner merges into {branch}
contest.empty: No fixes yet. Each helper works on its own branch and sends its fix here (propose_fix); they appear as rows to roll for.
contest.told: {name} was told to merge the fix into {branch}; the others were thanked. Vanilla Agents does not merge anything itself.
contest.stopped: You stopped this competition. No fix was picked.
contest.pick_quest: No competing quest picked. In the quest log, press Let several try on a quest, then Roll.
map.legend_heroes: a helper, in the zone it touched last (click: select)
contest.whisper_winner: Your fix for {title} was picked: merge it into {base} (branch {branch}). Thank you!
contest.whisper_other: Thanks for your fix for {title}. The owner picked another one, so you can stop working on it and leave your branch as it is.
guide.compete_1: For a tricky quest, press Let several try in the quest log and choose 2, 3 or 4 tries. Up to that many helpers may each make their own fix, on their own branch.
guide.compete_2: Helpers send their fix with the propose_fix tool: a short summary and their branch or git worktree. Their raid frames show crossed swords while they compete.
guide.compete_3: Press Roll on the quest to open the Need or Greed window: one row per fix with the helper's picture, summary, files changed and the checker's verdict. Check this one runs the project's checks on that branch; Show changes opens it in Inspect.
guide.compete_4: Need picks the winner (only you can; helpers have no way to). The winner is told by whisper to merge the fix into the base branch, the others are thanked, and the dice roll is just for show. Vanilla Agents never merges anything itself.
guide.compete_5: Pass hides a fix for now; Stop competing ends the competition without a winner.
guide.compete_6: In the inn, the competing helpers gather at one big table with their laptops open, facing each other, until you decide. The winner cheers when you pick it, the others applaud. Needed at the quest board or being checked? That comes first.
guide.worldmap_4: Helpers appear as small portraits in the zone of the file they touched last, pulsing while they work. Hover one for its name, click it to select that helper.
guide.worldmap_5: A zone with a helper in it is always at least explored: files in a helper's own git worktree and paths written relative to the project count too, files outside the project do not.
integ.title: Integrations
integ.desc: Bring work in from GitHub, Jira or Linear as bounties on the Bounty Board (H). Nothing becomes a quest until you press Make it a quest there.
integ.privacy: Tokens and keys stay in your own settings file on this PC and go only to that service. They are never shown here again in full.
integ.github_desc: Open issues and pull requests of the open project's GitHub repository, plus its latest CI runs in the quest log.
integ.secret_saved: Saved (ends in {word}). Leave empty to keep it.
integ.secret_saved_short: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
integ.labels_hint: bug, good first issue (empty = every open issue)
integ.signed_in_count: Signed in as {name} via {tool}. {count} on the Bounty Board.
integ.files_desc: Export a CSV file from Jira (Filters > Export > CSV) or Linear (Settings > Import / Export > Export CSV) and import it here. No keys needed.
integ.imported: {count} bounties from {name} are on the Bounty Board. Finished rows skipped: {n}.
integ.too_big: That file is too big (more than {n} KB). Export fewer rows.
integ.demo: Demo data is on (developer setting VANILLA_INTEGRATIONS_FAKE): GitHub answers from a test file, not from github.com.
auction.made: Quest made: {title}. Approve it in the quest log as usual.
auction.empty_imported: Nothing imported yet. Switch on GitHub, or import a Jira or Linear file, in Options > Integrations.
auction.count_imported: {count} imported proposals. Each becomes a quest only when you say so.
ci.label: CI
guide.integrations_1: Options > Integrations > Import from GitHub brings the open project's open issues and pull requests to the Bounty Board (H), on the Imported tab. It is off until you switch it on.
guide.integrations_2: Sign in with the gh command (run gh auth login once in a terminal) or paste a read-only token. Choose which labels and which pull requests, and how often to refresh.
guide.integrations_3: Imported items are only proposals: helpers cannot see or take them. Press Make it a quest on one to turn it into a normal quest whose why starts with GitHub and the link; you approve it in the quest log as usual.
guide.integrations_4: When an issue is closed on GitHub, its proposal leaves the board at the next refresh. A quest you already made from it stays.
guide.ci_1: With GitHub import on and workflows in the project, the quest log shows a CI line under quests in progress or ready, for example CI: build passed 4 min ago, and the system monitor gets a CI row.
guide.ci_2: CI is extra information only. A quest is still checked by your own checker; a red CI line means have a look, not stop.
guide.jira_linear_1: Export a CSV file from Jira or Linear and press Import from file in Options > Integrations. Open rows become proposals on the Bounty Board; finished rows are skipped. No keys are needed.
guide.jira_linear_2: If you prefer, Linear (personal API key) and Jira Cloud (e-mail and API token) can also be fetched by themselves every few minutes. Keys stay in your settings file and go only to that service.
addons.title: AddOns
addons.reload_hint: Changes take effect when the window reloads.
addons.empty: No addons yet. Install a .zip, or copy an addon folder into the addons folder.
addons.pick: Pick an addon on the left to see what it does.
addons.perm_state: Reads the live picture: helpers, quests, chat lines and changed file names.
addons.perm_panel: Adds its own small window or sign to the screen.
addons.perm_inn: Draws on, or changes, the inn or workshop view.
addons.perm_chat: Reads or adds lines in the chat window (in this window only; never sent to Claude).
addons.perm_actions: Presses buttons that change things: Verify, approve, whisper helpers, start quests.
addons.perm_network: Talks to other websites on the internet.
addons.perm_legacy: An old-style addon says nothing about itself. Like every addon, it can do anything the window can.
addons.trust: Every addon runs inside this window with the window's full power, whatever it says above. Only enable addons you wrote or trust.
addons.no_license_file: No LICENSE file in the folder: the Workshop can only link to it, not host a copy.
addons.remove_sure: Move {name} to the .removed folder? Nothing is deleted.
addons.pkg_rehost: The licence {text} lets the Workshop host a copy, so players can install it with one click.
addons.pkg_link: The licence {text} is not on the Workshop's list, so it will be listed as a link to you, not hosted.
addons.submit_1: Pull request: in the Open Vanilla repository on GitHub, add {file} to workshop/catalog/ and the zip to workshop/agents/.
addons.submit_2: Or upload: on the Workshop page choose Share an addon and pick the zip, licence and one-line summary (once uploads are open).
addons.submit_3: A person at the Workshop reviews every addon before anyone can install it.
addons.installed: Installed {name} {version}. It stays off until you enable it.
addons.exists: An addon with this id is installed already. Replace it? The old one is moved to the .removed folder.
addons.too_big: That file is too big for an addon (at most {n} KB).
addons.browse_title: Open Vanilla Workshop: Vanilla Agents addons
addons.browse_note: Browse goes online to the Workshop (openvanilla.app) only when you click it. Nothing else about addons uses the internet.
addons.browse_empty: No Vanilla Agents addons in the Workshop yet. Be the first: package yours and send it in.
guide.addons_3: Install from .zip checks the file first (no tricks with folder names, no huge files) and never overwrites an addon unless you choose Replace. Remove moves it to the .removed folder; nothing is deleted.
guide.addon_share: Share an addon in the Workshop
guide.addon_share_1: Package for the Workshop makes a zip and a catalogue entry in the addons/.packages folder and says how to send them to the Open Vanilla Workshop.
guide.addon_share_2: Browse the Workshop lists Vanilla Agents addons others have shared. It goes online only when you click it; a download is checked against the Workshop's fingerprint before it is installed.
guide.set_addons_1: Options > Vanilla Agents > AddOns opens the AddOns window: switch each addon on or off, read what it says it does, install, remove or package it. Reload the window to apply.
party.share_hint: Send a link to your friends. When they click it, a page with a Join button opens, and their Vanilla Agents asks them to confirm.
load.slow: The first start builds the inn for your graphics card, so it takes longest. Next time is quicker.
load.helpers: {count} helpers are already in the inn
welcome.title: Welcome to the inn
welcome.helpers: Every Claude Code session walks in here as a helper and works at a laptop. You see what it is doing on its screen.
welcome.move: Walk with W A S D, look around with the right mouse button, and click a helper to talk to it.
welcome.quests: Work arrives as quests in the Quest log (L). Nothing starts until you approve it, and a checker runs your tests before a quest counts as done.
welcome.party: Working with friends who also have helpers? Press G, host a party and send them the link.
claudelink.title: Connect Claude
claudelink.intro: Every Claude you connect walks into the inn as a helper. Connect the ones you use; each takes one click.
claudelink.code_what: Your terminal and editor sessions. Each one shows up as a helper and can use the Vanilla Agents tools.
claudelink.desktop_what: Chats and tasks in the Claude app on this PC can start quests and report progress to the inn.
claudelink.web_what: A Claude on claude.ai or your phone joins through Browser access, as a custom connector.
claudelink.on_seen: Connected. {count} sessions came in, the last {when}.
claudelink.on_none: Connected. Start a Claude Code session and it walks in here.
claudelink.elsewhere: Connected to another copy of Vanilla Agents. Reconnect to point it here.
claudelink.partial: Sessions come in, but Claude Code does not have the Vanilla Agents tools yet. Reconnect to add them.
claudelink.code_missing: Claude Code is not installed on this PC.
claudelink.desktop_missing: The Claude desktop app is not installed on this PC.
claudelink.desktop_on: Connected. If you just connected it, quit and reopen the Claude app once.
claudelink.web_off: Not set up. It needs Browser access switched on.
claudelink.web_offline: Browser access is on but cannot reach the relay right now, so web Claudes cannot join yet.
claudelink.started: A terminal opened with Claude Code in {project}. Say hello: it walks in within a few seconds.
claudelink.copy_cmd: Or type this in a terminal: {text}
claudelink.help: How do I know it worked? A new helper walks in and sits at a laptop as soon as a connected Claude starts.
claudelink.welcome_line: Connect Claude first: Esc > Connect Claude (or the button below).
